column2: The get of Vlad von Carstein, the bloodline that would rule the living as a lord rules his serfs. The Court of Sylvania hides behind the masks of mortal nobility until the night it is ready to march, and then the dead march with it. Its masters prize strength, cunning and the patience to wait out the centuries.
The Master of Court commands every von Carstein, and in the end the dead of Sylvania themselves.

The knightly order of the Blood Dragons, founded in the Blood Keep by Walach Harkon. Abhorash taught that the curse is mastered by perfection in battle, and his get seek that perfection through duel and quest, scorning the schemes of lesser bloodlines. Honour is everything to a Blood Dragon, and a knight who loses it is cast back down among the squires.
The Grand Master of the Ordo Draconis leads the knights of the Blood Keep and judges every challenge.

The daughters of Neferata, Queen of Lahmia. The Sisters rule from behind thrones, in the beds and ears of princes, and few mortals ever learn that the beautiful woman at court is centuries dead. From the Silver Pinnacle the Queen of Mysteries spins a web that reaches every court of the Old World.
The Queen of Mysteries is the voice of Neferata, and every Sister owes her obedience and favour.

The heirs of W'soran, scholars of death who care nothing for the world of the living except as material. In their towers they labour for centuries over a single work, and their greatest dream is to finish what Nagash began. A Necrarch is judged by what they have learned, and by what they have made.
The Lords of the Dark Tower are the greatest minds of the bloodline, and W'soran is first among them.

The cursed descendants of Ushoran, last king of Strygos, whose realm the orcs and the Nagashi threw down. The Strigoi are outcasts, hated by the other bloodlines and hunted by the living, and they live among graveyards with their ghoul courts. Yet they remember that they were once kings, and some dream of Strygos reborn.
The Heir of Ushoran would be the first king of the Strigoi since Strygos fell.

Long ago the Dragon Emperor poisoned the serpent-kin of the east, and they should have died. The Dark Crystals kept them alive instead, and changed them into what they are now: more snake than man, cold of blood and patient as stone. The Jade Coil is the hidden mirror of Cathay, a court of mandarins and sages who serve nothing but their own hunger and the visions in the crystals.
The Serpent Sage gazes deepest into the Dark Crystals and speaks for the whole Coil.

The Mahtmasi have no kings and no hierarchy, only the eldest and the hungriest. They come when they are called, feeding on those who ask for them, loving and then devouring. They can become a swarm of flies and carrion birds, they eat their own kind, and they fear fire, sunlight and running water. The eldest of them keeps the gate of Gwingui, where the shadow realm touches the world.
The Big Bokor keeps the gate of Gwingui and is the closest thing the Carrion Children have to a master.
Claim a higher place in [Root.Society.GetName]. A vampire rises on deeds, standing and the trial of the bloodline. A living thrall can climb only so far.
Every bloodline tests those who would stand among its masters. Undertake the trial of [Root.Society.GetName].
The thirst never sleeps. Choose your prey.
Ask the Head of the Bloodline for Aid
You are at war, and the head of [Root.Society.GetName] has gold and the dead to spare. Ask for help, though they may refuse.
Your master thirsts. Offer your own veins, and rise in their esteem.
There are places your master cannot go: a temple, a market at noon, a guild hall in the sun. Go in their place.
Your liege is one of the undying. Take the faith of the vampires, swear yourself to their service, and become a thrall.
Has done a deed worthy of the bloodline (fed on worthy prey, answered a plea, served a master, won a duel), or holds the standing the bloodline expects
Is a vampire (living thralls rise no higher)
Is not a hidden von Carstein (throw off the mask first)
Has passed the trial of the bloodline
Is not already undertaking the trial
Has not failed the trial recently
Has not fed in the last two years
Has not asked for aid in the last ten years
The head of the bloodline is someone else, free and able
Has not offered blood in the last three years
Has not run an errand in the last five years
Feeding on the helpless shames a Blood Dragon.
The Mahtmasi feed on those who ask. Taking the unwilling is a poor offering.
A living servant of the undying, bound to a bloodline.
The thirst is quiet for now, and the blood runs strong.
Too much blood given, too little left.
The head of the bloodline has lent the dead of their lands to this war.
Sworn to the service of a vampire.

The court of Sylvania has taken note of you. Your name is spoken now in the halls of Drakenhof, and lesser vampires lower their eyes when you pass. You are [Root.GetSocietyRank] of the von Carstein line.
Before the knights of the Ordo Draconis you kneel and rise again as [Root.GetSocietyRank]. Abhorash taught that the curse is mastered only by perfection of the blade. You have come one step nearer.

A letter on scented paper, sealed in red wax with a serpent and a crown. The Sisters have weighed you and found you useful. You are [Root.GetSocietyRank] now, and the web of the Silver Pinnacle grows a thread tighter around the world.
The Brotherhood does not celebrate. A single page arrives, written in a hand that has not changed in five centuries, acknowledging that your work has merit. You are [Root.GetSocietyRank].

The ghouls howl in the graveyard and the bones are thrown. Among the outcast heirs of Strygos you are [Root.GetSocietyRank] now, and the others will remember it the next time the hunger drives them to your door.
You lay your coils before the Dark Crystal and the visions part to show you your own face, older and colder. The Jade Coil names you [Root.GetSocietyRank].
The Carrion Children have no thrones. But the flies settle on you a little more readily now, and the bokors whisper your name when they make their offerings. You are [Root.GetSocietyRank].

The thirst is upon you. Your servants keep a few souls fed and docile in the cellars for nights like this. But out in the dark there are warriors, hot-blooded and strong, whose blood would sing in your veins for years.

The thirst is upon you. There are servants in the cellars who would offer their necks without a word. Abhorash would call that the feeding of a beast. A Blood Dragon takes blood from those who can fight for it.

The hunger wakes you. Far off, someone has made an offering and spoken your name: a widow who wants a lover, a merchant who wants his rival dead, a mother who wants her child to live. They asked for you. They will have you, and you will have them.
A warrior, taken in the dark.

column1: Your humble [From.GetSocietyRank] is beset. My enemies press upon my lands and I have not the strength to throw them back alone. I beg the aid of our blood, in gold or in the dead of your domain, and I will remember the gift for as long as I walk.

column2: Send the dead of my lands.
Let them stand or fall alone.
A reply from [From.GetTitledName] has come, and with it help. The head of [Root.Society.GetName] has not forgotten their own.
The blood looks after its own.

column1: If you cannot hold your own lands you do not deserve them. Do not write to me again until you have something to offer.

column2: [From.GetTitledFirstName] kneels before you and bares [From.GetHerHis] throat. The thrall offers [From.GetHerHis] blood freely, as a servant should, and the pulse at [From.GetHerHis] neck beats fast.

Your master needs a letter carried into a temple, a debt collected in the market at noon, a priest bribed in his own chapel. These are places where no vampire can go, and so you go instead, smiling in the sun with the mark of the teeth hidden under your collar.
